name: fusion-project
description: Use when creating a Powerhouse Fusion project, deciding or verifying which Switchboard instance it should use as its backend, or starting and stopping its development server.
---

# Fusion Project

A Powerhouse Fusion project is a Next.js app (cloned from the `fusion-boilerplate` template) that talks to a Switchboard instance's GraphQL API as its only backend — it runs no reactor of its own. This skill covers creating one, choosing and verifying its Switchboard backend, and starting/stopping its dev server — always backgrounded, never blocking the session.

The Switchboard URL must be settled and verified live *before* the dev server starts, and must end in `/graphql`. Getting this wrong, or skipping verification, means the project silently fetches from the wrong backend, or fails to fetch anything at all.

## Quick reference

| Intent | Command |
|---|---|
| initialize | `git clone https://github.com/powerhouse-inc/fusion-boilerplate.git <name>`, rename in `package.json`, `pnpm install` — no `ph` CLI equivalent exists |
| obtain URL | read the target reactor's live output (see `reactor-project`), verify with a live GraphQL request — never a config default |
| start | write `PH_SWITCHBOARD_URL=<url>` to `.env` and export it, `NODE_ENV=development pnpm dev -p <port>` (port verified free first), as a background shell |
| stop | kill the *entire* descendant process tree you started; confirm the port used is free |

## References

- [Initialize a new project](references/00-initialize-project.md) — FPM.00
- [Obtain a Switchboard URL](references/01-obtain-switchboard-url.md) — FPM.01
- [Run and capture the endpoint](references/02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md) — FPM.02
- [Stop the project](references/03-stop-project.md) — FPM.03

## Common mistakes

- **Hunting for a `ph fusion` CLI command.** Doesn't exist. `ph init` scaffolds a reactor package, not a Fusion app. Clone the boilerplate instead (FPM.00.3).
- **Trusting `.env.example`'s `PH_SWITCHBOARD_URL` default.** Illustrative, not a value to copy — in a multi-instance environment it can point at an unrelated backend with no error until a query fails (FPM.01.3).
- **Skipping live verification of the Switchboard URL.** A config file or process argv can be stale; confirm with a live GraphQL request first (FPM.01.3).
- **Verifying with a bare `switchboard` CLI command.** Acts on its configured profile, which may default to a remote/cloud reactor. Use an explicit `--profile`; if none suitable exists, stop and tell the user the stanza to add — never edit `~/.switchboard/profiles.toml` yourself outside FPM.01.3's unattended exception.
- **Concluding the wiring is broken when `/` returns HTTP 500.** The boilerplate's homepage queries a `driveDocuments` field absent from current Switchboard schemas — a known app-level bug, not proof the URL is wrong (FPM.02.2).
- **Asserting a fixed port instead of reading the actual one.** Verify a port is free, background the server, and read its real `Local:` line rather than assuming `-p <port>` was honored (FPM.02.1/02.2).
- **Killing only the top-level PID, or by process name.** Leaves children running, or takes down an unrelated instance elsewhere. Enumerate and kill the whole descendant tree by PID (FPM.03.2).

## Reporting

Report the Switchboard URL and the Fusion URL to the user directly.

# Reference: 00-initialize-project.md

# FPM.00 Initialize a new Fusion Project

## FPM.00.1 Inspect existing projects

There is no project registry — the target parent directory (e.g. `/tmp/ph-smoke`) is the only source of truth.

- Check the target parent directory for an existing directory matching the project name. If one already exists, treat it as the existing project rather than creating a new one — see [03-stop-project.md](03-stop-project.md) if it needs to be stopped first.
- Confirm nothing is already bound to the port you intend to use before starting a new dev server (see [02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md](02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md)).

## FPM.00.2 Generate unique project name

- Create a suitable, descriptive project name in kebab case that reflects the target platform, for example `acme-portal`.
- If the name already exists, use the current date and time as suffix, e.g. `acme-portal-20260120-1635`.
- The name must match pattern: `/^[a-zA-Z0-9-_]+$/`.

## FPM.00.3 Initialize the project

There is no `ph` CLI command that creates a Fusion project — `ph --help` lists no `fusion` subcommand, and `ph init` scaffolds a reactor package project, not a Fusion app. Do not go hunting for one; it does not exist in this environment. The actual, working method is to clone the boilerplate and rename it in place:

```bash
cd <parent-dir>
git clone https://github.com/powerhouse-inc/fusion-boilerplate.git <name>
cd <name>
sed -i -e 's/fusion-boilerplate/<name>/g' package.json
pnpm install
```

- Confirm the clone succeeded and that `package.json`'s `"name"` field now reads `<name>`, not `fusion-boilerplate`.
- `pnpm install` must complete before starting the dev server (see [02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md](02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md)).
- Do not decide the Switchboard backend yet — that's [01-obtain-switchboard-url.md](01-obtain-switchboard-url.md), and it must be settled before the dev server starts.


---

# Reference: 01-obtain-switchboard-url.md

# FPM.01 Obtain a Switchboard URL for Fusion

Every Fusion project uses a Switchboard instance as its backend. You must identify the Switchboard URL _before_ running the Fusion project (see [02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md](02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md)). If you fail to provide a Switchboard URL, or provide the wrong one, the Fusion project will fetch the wrong data or fail to fetch any data at all.

## FPM.01.1 Consider which backend should be used

Review the context that is available to you to decide which backend should be used:
- Did the stakeholder explicitly provide a Switchboard URL?
- Did the stakeholder indicate which Switchboard instance should be used as backend?
- If the stakeholder didn't mention anything, are they indirectly expecting the Fusion platform to display data that is known to be in a particular Switchboard instance?

In terms of data, consider:
- Which document models and documents will be needed.
- If there are different environments available between which you need to choose: development, staging, or production.

Based on these considerations, decide to use:
- An existing Switchboard instance, potentially running in the cloud, with a public URL.
- A local reactor package project's Switchboard instance that you may need to start yourself.

## FPM.01.2 Start a Reactor Package project if needed

If the Switchboard instance is an existing instance running in the cloud, this step can be skipped.

If a local reactor package should function as backend, it must be started and running before you start the depending Fusion project. Use the `reactor-project` skill to start it (or confirm it's already running) and capture its Switchboard endpoint directly from that skill's own process output — do not assume the endpoint from a config file.

More than one reactor (or stale log from a previous run) is the normal case in this kind of environment, not an edge case — do not just pick whichever process, port, or log file you find first. Match the candidate process's argv or working directory against the target project's own path (e.g. a `cd /path/to/<project> && ph vetra ...` command line, or a log whose surrounding directory is that project's) before trusting its Switchboard URL. If a log looks stale (an old timestamp, or no corresponding live process), discard it and keep looking rather than using it.

## FPM.01.3 Identify and verify the Switchboard URL

Ensure the Switchboard URL is in the required format: `http(s)://domainname[:port]/graphql`, for example `http://localhost:4101/graphql` or `https://switchboard.cloudhosting.tld/graphql`. Add the `/graphql` path if it's missing — without it the Fusion project will fail to fetch its data.

Get the URL from the target reactor's own live process output (its log or startup banner) — never assume it from a config file or template default. In particular: **the fusion-boilerplate's own `.env.example` ships `PH_SWITCHBOARD_URL=http://localhost:4001/graphql` as an illustrative default, and it is a trap.** In an environment with more than one Powerhouse instance running, that port can belong to a completely unrelated instance. Copying it uncritically would silently wire the Fusion project to the wrong backend, with no error until a query actually fails.

Before wiring the URL in, verify it is actually live with a real GraphQL request:
```bash
curl -s -X POST <switchboard-url> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"{__typename}"}'
```
An HTTP 200 response confirms the endpoint is live. Do this even when the URL came from a source you trust — verify, don't assume.

Do not verify with a bare `switchboard` CLI command. It acts on its currently configured profile, which may default to a remote/cloud reactor, and can return a plausible-looking result while silently reading a completely different backend. If a later step needs the `switchboard` CLI itself, it must be invoked with an explicit `--profile <name>` bound to this instance. Check whether a suitable profile already exists with `switchboard config list`. If none targets this Switchboard URL, **stop** and tell the user the exact stanza to add themselves to `~/.switchboard/profiles.toml`, for example:
```toml
[profiles.local]
url = "http://localhost:<port>/graphql"
```
`switchboard init` requires an interactive TTY and takes no flags to run non-interactively — creating a profile is normally a one-time setup step for the user, and silently rewriting `~/.switchboard/profiles.toml` yourself remains forbidden whenever a human is reachable to confirm it. The sole exception — an unattended run with no human available to confirm — is the same one documented in the `reactor-project` skill's RPPM.01.2 (`references/01-run-and-capture-endpoint.md`): only then may you append the stanza yourself, and only if you then clearly report that you did so and the exact stanza you wrote.

Report the verified Switchboard URL to the user.


---

# Reference: 02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md

# FPM.02 Run the project and capture the Fusion endpoint

## FPM.02.1 Start the project and wait until it's ready

Pass the verified Switchboard URL from FPM.01 via a `.env` file in the project root — `next dev` loads it automatically:
```bash
printf 'PH_SWITCHBOARD_URL=<switchboard-url>\n' > .env
```
Also export it in the shell environment of the start command itself. This is redundant with the `.env` file, but it is the combination that was confirmed to work:
```bash
NODE_ENV=development PH_SWITCHBOARD_URL=<switchboard-url> pnpm dev -p <port>
```

Never assert a fixed port. Verify a candidate port is free first (e.g. `ss -ltn | grep -E ':<port>\b'` — anchor with `\b`, since an unanchored `grep :<port>` also matches a longer port that merely starts with it, e.g. `:3000` matching `:30001`), then start the command above as a **backgrounded** shell. Never run it in the foreground — it is a persistent dev server that does not exit on its own, and foregrounding it blocks the session.

Read the background shell's accumulated output, polling every 2-3 seconds for up to 90 seconds, until it prints Next.js's dev-server banner line — of the form `- Local:         http://localhost:<port>` (note the leading `- ` and the padding before the URL; match on `Local:` rather than the exact spacing). This is the real readiness signal — do not treat a fixed sleep, or the process merely being alive, as proof of readiness.

## FPM.02.2 Parse and verify the Fusion endpoint

From the log, read the actual `Local:` line and report that observed URL — not the port you passed with `-p`, even if the two happen to agree.

**Known incompatibility — this is an application bug, not a wiring problem.** The fusion-boilerplate's stock homepage (`app/page.tsx`) queries a `driveDocuments` field that does not exist on current Switchboard schemas (which offer `findDocuments`/`document` instead), producing an HTTP 500 on `/`. If you see this 500, it does not mean the Switchboard URL is wrong — quite the opposite: a schema-mismatch GraphQL error is itself proof that the Fusion dev server reached the live Switchboard. Do not conclude the wiring is broken and start debugging a correctly configured Switchboard URL. Leave the homepage query as-is; fixing generated application code is out of scope here. This matters because later work builds pages on this same boilerplate, and mistaking this for a wiring failure would send that work down the wrong path.

Report the Fusion URL — and this known 500 caveat, if it occurred — to the user.


---

# Reference: 03-stop-project.md

# FPM.03 Stop the project

## FPM.03.1 Verify project is running

- Check whether the background shell started in [02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md](02-run-and-capture-endpoint.md) is still alive.
- The PID captured at start time (e.g. a shell's `$!`) is often not the actual server — `pnpm dev` runs several layers deep (pnpm itself, under Node, under the Next.js dev server process). Enumerate the full descendant tree with `pstree -p <captured-pid>` or `ps --ppid <captured-pid>` (repeated down the chain) before shutting anything down. **Never group-kill the shell's PGID** (e.g. `kill -- -<pgid>`) — that PGID is routinely shared with the tool's own persistent shell, and killing it kills your own session, even if you've verified the PGID's members first. Kill only the individually enumerated descendant PIDs.
- If it is not running, skip to confirming the port is free (FPM.03.2 below).

## FPM.03.2 Shutdown the project

- Kill **every process in the descendant tree** you enumerated above — one captured PID is not enough, and commonly leaves children (pnpm, the Next.js server process) running, reparented to PID 1.
- Never kill by process name or pattern (e.g. `pkill -f "next dev"` or `pkill -f pnpm`). An unrelated Powerhouse instance may be running elsewhere on this machine, and a name-based kill would take it down too. Only kill PIDs you individually enumerated as descendants of the process you started.
- After killing, confirm the port you actually used is free. Never assert a fixed port number — use whichever port you verified free and started with in FPM.02.1:
  ```bash
  ss -ltn | grep -E ':<port>\b'
  ```
  (anchor with `\b` — an unanchored `grep :<port>` also matches a longer port that merely starts with it, e.g. `:3000` matching `:30001`.) An empty result is necessary but not sufficient — also re-issue the same kind of live request used in FPM.02.2 against the Fusion URL and confirm it no longer responds. If it still responds, either a descendant survived (enumerate again) or the port belongs to a process you did not start — in the latter case leave it alone and do not report the project as stopped.
- Confirm any unrelated pre-existing process on the machine is still present and untouched.
